title.en: Avoir + past participle: telling what happened

summary.en: Combine a short helper form of avoir with an action's past participle.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 1 and 6.

Throughout the week speakers report completed events with two-word verb groups: *Quelqu'un a sonné* ('Someone rang'), *Quelqu'un à la gare a pris ma valise* ('Someone at the station took my suitcase'), and *j'ai sauvé* ('I saved').

A present form of *avoir* (*ai*, *as*, *a*, *avons*, *avez*, *ont*) pairs with a past participle. Regular -er verbs form participles in `-é` (*sonné*, *sauvé*), while common irregular verbs have crisp short forms worth learning directly, such as *pris* from *prendre*.

Not every French verb uses *avoir* in the past (arrival and movement verbs like *venir* and *arriver* use *être*), so listen to the helper and participle as a single unit.

On replay, catch the tiny vowel of *j'ai* or *a* right before *sonné*, *pris*, and *sauvé*.
